cases.visibleGeometry: A compact cluster of angular high spots and short straight edges occupies the northwest quadrant, with one detached small knob south of it. A faint curving track passes just east. Another low rise sits farther south. The sharp cluster is consistent across illumination directions.
cases.alternatives: Exposed bedrock, rubble, recent clearance or dumped material near a track; some sharp edges and gaps may reflect ground classification around objects.
cases.supportLimits: The angular cluster contains many interpolated cells, so its internal edges cannot be trusted as measured ground. The surrounding terrain is mostly supported.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns, imagery and nearby mapped features to separate rock, recent rubble and built geometry.

cases.visibleGeometry: A broad sinuous slope break runs west to east across the upper half, separating rougher northern ground from a smoother southern surface. Small isolated hummocks occur on both sides. No coherent enclosure or platform is apparent.
cases.alternatives: Natural slope or drainage edge, vegetation-related ground-model noise, erosion and field alteration; many northern speckles coincide with interpolation.
cases.supportLimits: Interpolation is dense along the break and around several hummocks. The broad form is visible, but fine outlines are uncertain.

cases.visibleGeometry: Regular parallel cultivation bands fill the western and southern fields. A straight north-south boundary meets an east-west linear bank or ditch near the centre. A second east-west field edge crosses the northeast. The intersection has a small raised irregularity.
cases.alternatives: Field boundaries, track drainage and agricultural terracing explain the straight lines and repeated bands. The small junction rise may be a gate, vegetation or model interpolation.
cases.supportLimits: Most field surfaces are measured, but the boundaries and junction have narrow interpolated strips. Their fine cross-sections need source-return checks.

cases.visibleGeometry: A long straight east-west depression or bank crosses the lower half, and a parallel field edge crosses the upper quarter. Repeated cultivation lines extend beyond them. A small isolated mound appears near the upper edge at roughly x310, y98.
cases.alternatives: Agricultural boundaries, drainage, track grading and vegetation or stone piles are plausible. The small mound may be an isolated rock or agricultural debris.
cases.supportLimits: The linear edges coincide with interpolated strips; the small mound is surrounded by measured terrain but its crest requires raw returns. No bounded arrangement is evident.
